place.zh: 沉鼎山 · 后山崖顶 · 青石前
place.en: Mount Chending · The cliff top · before the blue stone

setup.zh: 瞿老捧出一个旧布包：半卷竹简，《河洛剑诀》。三百年，没有一个人练成过第一宫。「你念开篇。」
setup.en: Elder Qu brings out an old cloth bundle: half a bamboo scroll, the He-Luo Sword Canon. In three hundred years no one has mastered its first palace. "Read the opening."

recap.zh: 剑诀开篇是娘教的洛书口诀。瞿老问：「……你娘，是谁？」临了只一句：那颗丹，吃之前，先来问我。
recap.en: The canon opened with the Luo rhyme your mother taught you. Elder Qu asked: "…Who is your mother?" And at the last: that pill — before you eat it, come and ask me.

zh: 半卷竹简，比《吐纳经》还旧。
en: Half a bamboo scroll, older than the Scroll of Breath.
"Nine on the head, one on the feet, three on the left, seven on the right…"

story.zh:
跟着进屋捧出一个旧布包，一层一层打开，是半卷竹简，比《吐纳经》还旧：「本观祖师留下的一门剑诀。三百年，没有一个人练成过一宫。它要五行俱全，一行不缺，剑气才转得起来。五行杂灵根，天底下都笑的那种。我等了五十年。」

小满胸口的木牌烫了一下，银月钻了出来，蹲在他肩膀上，看了看瞿老，看了看竹简，眯起眼睛：「……本王的徒弟，他也配？」小满吓得一哆嗦，险些一屁股坐在香炉上。瞿老往他肩膀上看了一眼，什么都没看见，又看了一眼：「你肩膀上，有东西？」小满忙道：「……有、有只虫子。」银月大怒：「你说谁是虫子？！」木牌随即凉了——她走的时候，隔着衣裳，狠狠地踩了他锁骨一脚。

瞿老没再问，把竹简推到他面前：「《河洛剑诀》。你念开篇。」
story.en:
Then he went into the hut and brought out an old cloth bundle and unwrapped it layer by layer: half a bamboo scroll, older than the Scroll of Breath. "A sword canon our founder left. In three hundred years no one has mastered a single palace of it. It needs all five elements, not one missing, for the sword qi to turn. Five-element mixed roots — the kind the whole world laughs at. I've waited fifty years."

The token on Xiaoman's chest went hot, and Yinyue slipped out onto his shoulder, looked at Elder Qu, looked at the scroll, and narrowed her eyes: "…My disciple — and he thinks he's fit?" Xiaoman jumped so hard he nearly sat on the incense burner. Elder Qu looked at his shoulder, saw nothing, looked again: "Something on your shoulder?" "…A — a bug," said Xiaoman quickly. Yinyue was furious: "Who are you calling a bug?!" The token went cold at once — and as she left she stamped hard on his collarbone through his clothes.

Elder Qu asked no more, and pushed the scroll across to him: "The He-Luo Sword Canon. Read the opening."

exits.means: recites the opening of the sword canon

story.zh:
小满低头去看，手却停住了。竹简上的字，有些他认不全；可那几个字的排法——九个，三三一排，中间一个「五」——他实在太熟了。那是灶间的油灯底下，他娘拿九颗刻了记号的栗子，一颗一颗摆给他看的。他不用看竹简，便念了出来：「戴九履一，左三右七，二四为肩，六八为足，五居中央。」

崖顶上很静。一阵风吹过，香炉里三根香的烟一齐歪了一歪。瞿老脸上从来没有过什么表情，这一回，却有了：「……你没看竹简。」小满说：「我娘教的。她说，是她爹教她的。她爹，是从一本旧书上看来的。」瞿老沉默了很久很久，久到一截香灰无声无息地折断了，落在青石上。他才道：「……你娘，是谁？」

小满张了张嘴。他娘是谁？他娘是石坳村猎户家的媳妇，会织布，会算账，下雨天会把家里所有的盆都摆出来接水，一共十七个；他娘是一个落魄塾师的女儿，识字，嫁了一个不识字的猎户。他娘，还能是谁？他想了半天，只说出一句：「……我娘，是我外公的闺女。」瞿老看着他，嘴角动了一动，不知是想笑，还是想别的什么。他没有再问，把竹简卷起来，卷的时候，手指头在竹简的边上停了一停，像摸到了一道很旧的刻痕。

瞿老从脚边捡起一块扁扁的青石——泗水边上捡来的——拿扫帚把轻轻一敲。「当——」那一声不大，却很长，很远。小满心里忽然一动，好像在哪里听过这样的一声，想不起来了。「你是徐州人，」瞿老道，「九宫里，徐州是巽四。今日先教你巽四。」

他把扫帚倒过来握在手里，只动了一下。崖边积了一冬的落叶一片不剩，全给卷了起来，在半空里排成一个方方正正的格子，三三一排，共是九格，中间那一格空着；跟着纷纷落下，落成了一个字：**徐**。那个字，缺了中间一笔。瞿老把扫帚靠回墙角：「我练了四十年，只练到这一步。这剑诀，要五行一样生一样，在身子里转成一个圈。」他拿扫帚把在落叶上画了一个圈，点上五个点，又抹掉了一个，「我缺的是火。四十年，圈上总有一个口子。」

小满看着那个缺了一个点的圈，想起秘境石室里，他身子里转起来的那一圈灶火。原来这天底下，漏的不止他一个。瞿老扛起扫帚往草屋里走，头也不回：「你五行俱全。你把它填上，再来找我。」

走到门口，他又停住了，背对着小满，道：「那颗丹。」小满道：「是。」瞿老道：「打算什么时候吃？」小满道：「练到九层圆满。」瞿老沉默了一会儿：「……那颗丹，吃之前，先来问我。」说罢，进了屋。

小满往山下走，走到半山腰，回头望了一眼。崖顶的草屋门开着，瞿老坐在那张木桌前，面前摆着那两只茶杯，一只朝上，一只朝下。他坐了很久，伸出手去，碰了碰那只朝下的杯子，碰了一碰，又缩了回来。那只杯子，还扣着。
story.en:
Xiaoman looked down, and his hand stopped. Some of the characters he couldn't read; but the arrangement — nine of them, three by three, a five in the middle — he knew too well. That was under the oil lamp in the kitchen, his mother laying out nine marked chestnuts for him one by one. He didn't need the scroll; he recited it: "Nine on the head, one on the feet, three on the left, seven on the right, two and four the shoulders, six and eight the feet, five in the middle."

The cliff top went very still. A breeze passed, and the three threads of smoke from the burner leaned together. Elder Qu's face had never shown anything; this time it did: "…You didn't look at the scroll." "My mother taught me. She said her father taught her. Her father got it from an old book." Elder Qu was silent a long, long time — so long that a stub of incense ash broke off without a sound and fell on the stone. Then he said: "…Your mother — who is she?"

Xiaoman opened his mouth. Who was his mother? A hunter's wife in Shi'ao Village who could weave and keep accounts and set out every basin in the house when it rained — seventeen of them; a poor village teacher's daughter who could read and married a hunter who couldn't. Who else could she be? After a long while all he could say was: "…My mother is my grandfather's daughter." Elder Qu looked at him, and the corner of his mouth moved — whether to laugh or something else, no one could tell. He asked no more, and rolled up the scroll; as he rolled it his finger paused on its edge, as if it had touched a very old notch.

Elder Qu picked up a flat bluestone from by his foot — picked up on the banks of the Si — and tapped it lightly with the broom handle. "Dang —" Not loud, but long, and far. Something stirred in Xiaoman, as if he'd heard a sound like that somewhere, and couldn't remember where. "You're a man of Xu," said Elder Qu. "Among the nine palaces, Xu is Xun Four. Today I teach you Xun Four first."

He turned the broom round in his hands and moved once. Every leaf that had gathered all winter at the cliff's edge was swept up and hung in the air in a square grid, three by three, nine squares, the middle one empty; then they drifted down and settled into one character: **Xu**. It was missing its middle stroke. Elder Qu leaned the broom against the wall: "Forty years' practice and this is as far as I got. This canon wants the five elements each giving birth to the next, turning in a ring inside you." With the broom handle he drew a circle on the leaves and dotted five points on it, then wiped one away. "What I lack is fire. Forty years, and my ring has always had a gap."

Xiaoman looked at the circle with a point missing and remembered the ring of stove-fire that had turned inside him in the hidden chamber. So he wasn't the only one in the world who leaked. Elder Qu shouldered the broom and went toward the hut without turning round: "You have all five. Fill it in, then come and find me."

At the door he stopped again, back to Xiaoman: "That pill." "Yes." "When do you mean to eat it?" "When I reach layer nine, complete." Elder Qu was silent a while: "…That pill — before you eat it, come and ask me first." And he went in.

Xiaoman went down the mountain, and halfway down looked back. The hut door stood open; Elder Qu sat at the wooden table with the two teacups before him, one up, one down. He sat a long time, then reached out and touched the upside-down cup — touched it once, and drew his hand back. The cup stayed face down.
